# Data sources and provenance

## Current release

**SIMULATED DATA — NOT LIVE NASA DATA.** Mission resources, crew state, radiation index, and a seeded scenario schedule are generated by the local educational model. One bundled NASA PDS browse product is available as read-only lunar-surface context; it is not ingested into or used by mission calculations. Other bundled NASA photographs, diagrams, and visualizations are credited contextual references, not mission measurements.

All current values are illustrative engineering assumptions for an educational exercise. The model assumptions, units, initial inventories, and limitations are documented in the root [README](../README.md) and in the in-app Data Source page. Lunar surface scenario estimates are never presented as cabin conditions.

## NASA Data Mode

NASA mission-data mode remains unavailable because the integrated product is not compatible with in-habitat life-support calculations. `src/data/dataConfig.js` keeps the mode disabled; the UI cannot switch simulated output to NASA data.

### NASA LRO Diviner archived surface-temperature browse product

- **Dataset/product:** LRO Diviner Derived Data Bundle, GHRM browse product `dghrm_tbol_m_70s70n_jpg`; global high-resolution mosaic of bolometric temperature at midnight.
- **Original source:** NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) Geosciences Node; Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Diviner Lunar Radiometer Experiment.
- **Product URL:** [PDS browse image](https://pds-geosciences.wustl.edu/lro/urn-nasa-pds-lro_diviner_derived1/browse/ghrm/dghrm_tbol_m_70s70n_jpg.jpg)
- **Product label:** [PDS metadata record](https://pds-geosciences.wustl.edu/lro/urn-nasa-pds-lro_diviner_derived1/browse/ghrm/dghrm_tbol_m_70s70n_jpg.xml)
- **Instrument/archive overview:** [LRO Diviner data sets](https://pds-geosciences.wustl.edu/missions/lro/diviner.htm)
- **Collection period:** 2009-07-05 through 2022-08-01, as stated in the PDS product label.
- **Spatial applicability:** Rendered lunar surface mosaic from 70°S to 70°N, not a single landing site.
- **Units and representation:** Bundled asset is the PDS JPEG browse rendering; it is a visual reference, not a calibrated numeric table. Consult the linked scientific products and their labels for quantitative values and units.
- **Limitations and use:** Historical lunar-surface observation only. The image is not real-time, a habitat temperature, crew exposure, or spacecraft-system measurement. It is not used to calculate mission parameters, resource balances, or crew health.

The source image is bundled at `public/data/nasa/diviner-midnight-global-mosaic.jpg` for reliable offline rendering. Its provenance and limits are catalogued in `src/data/nasaDataCatalog.js`. The in-app NASA Data Explorer labels it **REAL NASA DATA — HISTORICAL MEASUREMENTS** and explicitly states that no numeric measurements are extracted.

### Other official sources evaluated

- **NASA LRO CRaTER PDS bundle:** [urn:nasa:pds:lro-crater, version 1.6](https://pds.nasa.gov/ds-view/pds/viewBundle.jsp?identifier=urn%3Anasa%3Apds%3Alro-crater&version=1.6). Linked from the explorer, but no files were downloaded or decoded for this release. Calibrated product selection, units, quality flags, geometry, and shielded-habitat applicability require source-specific validation before use. The simulator does not infer a cabin dose from orbital observations.
- **NASA SVS 5027 south-pole illumination visualization:** [Illumination at the Moon’s South Pole to 80°S, 2025–2028](https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/5027). The NASA page says the visualization uses LRO LOLA terrain and JPL DE421 ephemeris. It is linked as external context, not bundled or used as a power forecast. No LOLA numerical terrain or illumination time-series data are integrated.

These are source links only, not loaded datasets. The explorer distinguishes them from the locally bundled Diviner browse image.

## Bundled NASA visual references

The application bundles the following NASA imagery locally to avoid third-party hotlinks. Their source links, image credits, alt text, and intended-use caveats are maintained in [`src/data/visualAssetCatalog.js`](../src/data/visualAssetCatalog.js). They are not inputs to mission calculations. A NASA photograph or illustration does not imply NASA endorsement of LunarBase.

All local visual references use descriptive alternative text, lazy loading, asynchronous decoding, visible image-load fallbacks, and source links. ISS hardware is contextual, not a claim about a lunar habitat design. Image assets are not used to derive measured values.

## Integration boundaries

- `src/data/nasaDataCatalog.js` records provenance for the read-only NASA archive image shown in the app.
- `src/data/nasaDataAdapter.js` validates and adapts an explicitly verified external dataset; it does not fetch data.
- `src/data/dataValidator.js` checks mission-state invariants and required external provenance metadata.
- `src/data/unitConverter.js` converts a limited set of compatible engineering units.
- `src/data/dataNormalizer.js` maps keyed measurements into requested internal units.
- `src/data/simulationDataProvider.js` provides the local educational simulation separately from external data.

`src/data/simulationDataGenerator.js` creates a reproducible scenario order from a stored seed. The seed changes event order, not the underlying stated causes or values; this is not a probability or lunar-weather model.

No live NASA API response or measurement is fabricated. NASA mission-data mode remains unavailable because the only bundled product is a rendered lunar-surface image and the linked sources are not integrated. A future acquisition layer and source-specific compatibility checks must be implemented and tested before mission calculations can be switched to external data.

## Adjustable educational model

The Settings page exposes per-person oxygen, gross water, and packaged-food rates; baseline habitat power; solar generation; recycling efficiency; and new-mission starting inventories. Changes to model rates apply to the active mission’s upcoming operation and persist locally; previous history remains unchanged. Each allowed range is validated and the form previews the resulting baseline daily resource model. Crew specialist values and the engineering repair-cost bonus are also illustrative game mechanics—not measured human performance or validated vehicle specifications.
